Proposition 1
items.title: California Veteran and Housing Assistance Programs Bond Measure
items.summary: Issue $11.25 billion in bonds to fund Multifamily Housing Program, CalVet Home Loan Program, and youth housing
items.pro: A "yes" vote supports authorizing the state to issue $11.25 billion in bonds to fund income-qualified housing programs, such as the Multifamily Housing Program, the CalHome Program, and the Joe Serna, Jr. Farmworker Housing Grant Program, and the veteran home loan program.
items.con: A "no" vote opposes authorizing the state to issue $11.25 billion in bonds to fund income-qualified housing programs, such as the Multifamily Housing Program, the CalHome Program, and the Joe Serna, Jr. Farmworker Housing Grant Program, and the veteran home loan program.

items.name: Proposition 2
items.title: California Budget Stabilization Account Cap Increase and Gann Limit Changes Amendment
items.summary: Increase the Budget Stabilization Account (BSA) cap from 10% of general fund revenue to 20% and excluding deposits into the BSA from the Gann Limit
items.pro:
A "yes" vote supports this amendment to:

  • increase the Budget Stabilization Account (BSA) cap from 10% to 20% of estimated general fund proceeds of taxes;
  • increase deposits into the BSA by counting capital gains revenue above 10% of general fund proceeds of taxes at 150% of its value in the deposit calculation; extend through the 2039-40 fiscal year the requirement that half of those funds be appropriated for debts and liabilities, and add federal loans to the state's Unemployment Fund to the eligible obligations;
  • exclude deposits into the BSA and the Projected Surplus Temporary Holding Account from the Gann Limit, while counting withdrawals against it; and
  • provide that the governor's May budget revision constitutes a proclamation of a budget emergency when the conditions for one exist.
items.con: A "no" vote opposes this amendment to change rules governing the state's rainy day fund, extra debt repayment, and fiscal state of emergencies.

items.name: Proposition 3
items.title: California Renew State Income Tax Increase for Education Funding Initiative
items.summary: Renew the additional income taxes enacted with the approval of Proposition 38 in 2012 that fund education and early childhood programs.
items.pro: A "yes" vote supports amending the state constitution to indefinitely extend the top marginal tax rates set to expire in 2031 on single filers earning at least $361,000 or joint filers earning at least $721,000, with 89% of revenue allocated to K–12 schools and 11% to community colleges.
items.con: A "no" vote opposes amending the state constitution to indefinitely extend the top marginal tax rates on single filers earning at least $361,000 or joint filers earning at least $721,000, thereby allowing them to expire in 2031.

items.name: Proposition 4
items.title: California Allow Public Financing of Election Campaigns Measure
items.summary: Allow the state and local governments to create programs that provide candidates with public funds under spending limits and eligibility rules
items.pro: A "yes" vote supports repealing the ban on public financing of campaigns, enacted in 1988, and allowing the state and local governments to create programs that provide candidates with public funds under spending limits and eligibility rules.
items.con: A "no" vote opposes repealing the ban on using public funds for election campaigns, keeping the prohibition in place with the existing exemption for charter cities.

items.name: Proposition 5
items.title: California Eliminate State Officer Recall Successor Elections Amendment
items.summary: Eliminate the successor election when a state officer is recalled, thereby leaving the office vacant until it is filled according to state law
items.pro:
A "yes" vote supports amending the state constitution to:

  • eliminate the simultaneous election of a successor when a state officer is recalled, thereby leaving the office vacant until it is filled according to state law;
  • allow the recalled officer to run again for the same office at the special election, if one is held; and
  • authorize the lieutenant governor to fill a gubernatorial vacancy until the expired term, unless the vacancy occurred before the close of the nomination period for the next statewide election during the first two years of the governor’s term, then a special election would be called and the winner would serve the remainder of the term.
items.con: A "no" vote opposes this amendment, thereby maintaining the requirement that a simultaneous election to fill the statewide office vacancy be held at the time of the recall election.

items.name: Proposition 37
items.title: California Second Mortgage Homebuyer Program and Revenue Bond Initiative
items.summary: Establish a second mortgage homebuyer program for qualified homebuyers on qualifying homes and issue $25 billion in bonds to fund the program
items.pro:
A "yes" vote supports this initiative to:

  • establish a second mortgage homebuyer program for qualified homebuyers — defined as California residents of at least one year who earn at or below 200% of the area median income for a similar-sized family in the county or city where the home is located and provide a down payment of at least 3% of the purchase price — on qualifying homes administered by the California Housing Finance Agency (CalHFA), and
  • authorize the CalHFA to issue up to $25 billion in bonds to fund the program.
items.con: A "no" vote opposes this initiative to establish a second mortgage homebuyer program.

items.name: Proposition 38
items.title: Establish Immunology and Immunotherapy Research Institute Initiative
items.summary: Establish an Immunology and Immunotherapy Research Institute affiliated with the University of California
items.pro:
A "yes" vote supports an initiative to:

  • authorize the state to issue $8.4 billion in general obligation bonds to fund immunology and immunotherapy research;
  • establish an Immunology and Immunotherapy Research Institute affiliated with the University of California; and
  • award grants to California-based public and nonprofit medical research institutions for immunology and immunotherapy research.
items.con: A "no" vote opposes this initiative to issue $8.4 billion in bonds to fund research and development treatments using immunology and immunotherapy.

items.name: Proposition 39
items.title: California Voter Identification, Citizenship Verification, and Registered Voter List Administration Initiative
items.summary: Require voters to present government-issued identification when casting ballots and require election officials to use government data to confirm voter citizenship and report verification rates
items.pro:
A "yes" vote supports this ballot initiative to:

  • require voters to present a government-issued ID for in-person voting or provide the last four digits of a government-issued ID designated during voter registration for mail-in voting;
  • require election officials to "maintain accurate voter registration lists [and]... use best efforts to verify citizenship attestations using government data” and to report each year the percentage of each county’s voter rolls that have been citizenship-verified;
  • require the State Auditor to audit government compliance with these requirements during odd-numbered years and report “findings and recommendations for improving the integrity of elections to the public.”
items.con:
A "no" vote opposes this ballot initiative, leaving existing law in place, under which:

  • voters are not required to present a government-issued ID when voting; and
  • voters must attest to their citizenship under penalty of perjury and provide identifying information when registering; election officials are not required to use government data to verify those attestations or to report citizenship verification rates.

items.name: Proposition 40
items.title: California One-Time Wealth Tax for State-Funded Healthcare, Education, and Food Assistance Programs Initiative
items.summary: Levy a one-time 5% tax on the accumulated wealth, including shares of capital stock, bonds or other evidences of indebtedness, and any legal or equitable interest, of billionaires in the state to fund state-funded health care programs, such as Medi-Cal
items.pro: A "yes" vote supports this initiative to levy a one-time 5% tax on the accumulated wealth, including shares of capital stock, bonds or other evidences of indebtedness, and any legal or equitable interest, of billionaires in the state to fund state-funded health care programs, such as Medi-Cal, and state food assistance and public education.
items.con: A "no" vote opposes this initiative to levy a one-time 5% tax on the accumulated wealth, including shares of capital stock, bonds or other evidences of indebtedness, and any legal or equitable interest, of billionaires in the state to fund state-funded health care programs, such as Medi-Cal, and state food assistance and public education.

items.name: Proposition 41
items.title: California Prohibit Excluding New State Taxes from Spending Limit and Require Special Tax Audits Initiative
items.summary: Require state laws or ballot initiatives levying a new special tax enacted after January 1, 2026 to require the government entities or departments receiving revenue from the new tax to eliminate their lowest-performing programs and reinvest those savings in higher-performing programs
items.pro:
A "yes" vote supports this initiative to:

  • require pre-election audits for ballot initiatives proposing special taxes once they report collecting 25% of signatures to be included in the voter information pamphlet if it qualifies for the ballot;
  • require state laws or ballot initiatives levying a new special tax enacted after January 1, 2026, to undergo state audits every four years to determine program effectiveness and cost-saving measures; and
  • prohibit the state from enforcing any tax that is exempted or excluded from the state spending limit enacted or effective on or after January 1, 2026.
items.con: A "no" vote opposes this initiative to require an audit for state laws or ballot initiatives levying new special taxes after January 1, 2026.

items.name: Proposition 42
items.title: California Prohibit New Taxes on Retirement Holdings, Personal Assets, and Savings and Limit Retroactive Taxes Initiative
items.summary: Prohibit the enactment of new taxes after January 1, 2026 on ownership or accumulation of retirement holdings, individually-owned assets, and other forms of personal savings
items.pro:
A "yes" vote supports this initiative to amend the California Constitution to prohibit the enactment of:

  • new taxes after January 1, 2026, on ownership or control of retirement holdings, individually-owned assets, and other forms of personal savings, and
  • retroactive taxes that result in a tax liability based on conduct, activities, or a status that occurred or was present prior to the effective date of the tax.
items.con:
A "no" vote opposes this initiative to amend the California Constitution to prohibit the enactment of:

  • new taxes after January 1, 2026, on ownership or control of retirement holdings, individually-owned assets, and other forms of personal savings, and
  • retroactive taxes that result in a tax liability based on conduct, activities, or a status that occurred or was present prior to the effective date of the tax.

items.name: Proposition 43
items.title: California Two-Thirds Vote Requirement for Local Special Tax Initiatives and Property Tax Initiative Prohibition Amendment
items.summary: Require two-thirds vote by electorate to enact, extend, or increase local special tax initiatives and prohibit local governments and ballot initiatives from enacting ad valorem property taxes except those authorized elsewhere in the state constitution
items.pro: A "yes" vote supports this amendment to require a two-thirds vote by the electorate to enact, extend, or increase local special tax initiatives and prohibit local jurisdictions and ballot initiatives from enacting ad valorem property taxes, except for voter-approved bond debt-service taxes authorized elsewhere in the state constitution.
items.con: A "no" vote opposes this amendment to require a two-thirds vote by the electorate to enact, extend, or increase local special tax initiatives and prohibit local jurisdictions and ballot initiatives from enacting ad valorem property taxes, except for voter-approved bond debt-service taxes authorized elsewhere in the state constitution.

items.name: Proposition 44
items.title: California Spending Requirements for Federally Qualified Health Centers Initiative
items.summary: Prohibit healthcare clinics, specifically federally-qualified health centers and related organizations, from spending less than 90% of their annual revenue on mission-related purposes
items.pro: A "yes" vote supports this initiative to require nonprofit federally qualified health centers (FQHCs) and FQHC Look-Alikes to spend at least 90% of their annual total revenue on expenses that advance the health center's mission.
items.con: A "no" vote opposes this initiative to require nonprofit federally qualified health centers (FQHCs) and FQHC Look-Alikes to spend at least 90% of their annual total revenue on expenses that advance the health center's mission.

items.name: Proposition 45
items.title: Changes to Environmental Review Process for Certain Projects Initiative
items.summary: Establish timelines for local and state agencies to review plans and solicit public comment for essential projects, such as housing, improvements to water supply, transportation, energy, and facilities for health and public safety
items.pro:
A "yes" vote supports this initiative to make changes to the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) to:

  • establish deadlines for public agencies to complete environmental review and take required actions for projects deemed essential under the law;
  • limit public agencies' existing requirement to consider a range of project alternatives to reduce environmental impacts; and
  • change the court review process for project approvals by setting deadlines for filing and resolving lawsuits and limiting the evidence and relief the court can consider and order.
items.con: A "no" vote opposes this initiative to make changes to the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA), which governs state and local government agencies' review process for determining potential environmental impacts and mitigation solutions of proposed construction projects.

items.name: Measure A
items.title: Charter Changes Affecting Various City Departments and Commissions
items.summary: Amend the San Francisco Charter to remove outdated provisions and make  changes to the governance of local programs and departments
items.pro: A "yes" vote supports amending the San Francisco Charter to remove provisions that reference obsolete departments, require reliance on certain filing systems, and make other changes to the governance of local programs and departments.
items.con: A "no" vote opposes amending the San Francisco Charter to remove provisions that reference obsolete departments, require reliance on certain filing systems, and make other changes to the governance of local programs and departments.

items.name: Measure B
items.title: Establishing a Municipal Finance Corporation and a Public Bank
items.summary: Amend the San Francisco Charter to create a municipal finance corporation and a public bank
items.pro: A "yes" vote supports amending the San Francisco Charter to create a municipal finance corporation and a public bank that would exist as nonprofit corporations, each overseen by an oversight commission and board of directors.
items.con: A "no" vote opposes amending the San Francisco Charter to create a municipal finance corporation and a public bank.

items.name: Measure C
items.title: Contributions to the Housing Fund
items.summary: Change the method of annual contributions to the city's Housing Trust Fund
items.pro:
A "yes" vote supports amending the San Francisco City Charter to require that contributions to the Housing Trust Fund, beginning in 2028, be equal to the greater of the following, until the annual appropriation to the fund equals $125 million or more:

  • the amount equal to the past year's appropriation, plus 20% of the city's share of the 1% of ad valorem tax revenue resulting from the year-to-year increase; or
  • the amount equal to the past year's appropriation, adjusted by the percentage increase in the General Fund Discretionary Revenue budgeted for that year.
items.con: A "no" vote opposes amending the San Francisco City Charter to change the method of contributions to the Housing Trust Fund, thus maintaining that contributions be made each year in an amount equal to the past year's appropriation, adjusted by the percentage increase in the General Fund Discretionary Revenue budgeted for that year.

items.name: Measure D
items.title: Changes to Ballot Measure Process
items.summary: Make changes to the city's ballot measure referral and initiative process
items.pro:
A "yes" vote supports amending the San Francisco Charter to make the following changes to the ballot measure process:

  • eliminate the provision permitting the mayor or four members of the Board of Supervisors to place a measure on the ballot without a vote of the entire board;
  • require 8% of registered voters sign an initiative petition in order to place a measure on the ballot;
  • require 10% of registered voters sign a petition calling a special election on the ballot measure; and
  • allow proponents of a ballot measure to withdraw the initiative from the ballot up to 102 days before the election.
items.con:
A "no" vote opposes amending the San Francisco Charter, thus maintaining that:

  • a ballot measure can be placed on the ballot by either the mayor alone or by four members of the Board of Supervisors;
  • 2% of registered voters must sign an initiative petition to place a measure on the ballot;
  • a number of signatures equal to 10% of the number of voters for the Mayor in the last mayoral election must be filed in order to call a special election on a ballot measure; and
  • prohibit the withdrawal of an initiative petition at any time.

items.name: Measure E
items.title: City Administrator's Authority and Changes to City Contracting
items.summary: Require the Board of Supervisors to approve all city contracts that would generate more than $4.5 million or cost more than $25 million and amend the city administrator's roles and authority
items.pro:
A "yes" vote supports requiring the Board of Supervisors to approve all city contracts that would generate more than $4.5 million or cost more than $25 million, and amending the city administrator's roles and authority as follows:

  • grant the city administrator exclusive authority to propose ordinances governing procurement, and restrict the board from amending the ordinances;
  • increase the city administrator's term from five years to ten years;
  • declare that the city administrator's adopted procurement rules and regulations supersede conflicting department rules; and
  • permit the city administrator to implement a citywide policy for technology use.
items.con: A "no" vote opposes requiring the Board of Supervisors to approve all city contracts that would generate more than $4.5 million or cost more than $25 million, and amending the city administrator's roles and authority.

items.name: Measure F
items.title: Changes to Executive Branch Management
items.summary: Amend the structure of the executive branch of the city government and the authorities and duties of the mayor
items.pro:
A "yes" vote supports amending the San Francisco Charter to allow nomination boards to recommend only one or more names to the mayor for a position, permit appointing officials to remove their appointees in most departments without cause, and permit the mayor to:

  • reorganize executive branch departments, with some exceptions;
  • hire deputy mayors; and
  • hire and remove department heads.
items.con:
A "no" vote opposes amending the San Francisco Charter to allow nomination boards to recommend only one or more names to the mayor for a position, permit appointing officials to remove their appointees in most departments without cause, and permit the mayor to:

  • reorganize executive branch departments, with some exceptions;
  • hire deputy mayors; and
  • hire and remove department heads.

items.name: Measure G
items.title: Allowing Private Vehicles on the Great Highway in Sunset Dunes Park
items.summary: Open the Upper Great Highway to public vehicles on weekdays, except on holidays
items.pro: A "yes" vote supports permitting private vehicles to use the Upper Great Highway, except on weekends and government holidays.
items.con: A "no" vote opposes this measure, maintaining that the Upper Great Highway is closed to private vehicles seven days a week.

items.name: Measure H
items.title: Parcel Tax to Fund Public Muni Operations
items.summary: Implement a 15-year property tax to fund the San Francisco Municipal Transportation Agency
items.pro:
A "yes" vote supports creating a property tax, to be in effect from 2027 to 2042, to fund San Francisco Municipal Transportation Agency operations, with rates as follows:

  • for single-family residential parcels: a base tax of $129, an additional $0.42 per square foot of building area between 3,001 and 5,000 square feet, and an additional $1.99 per square foot of building area above 5,000 square feet;
  • for multifamily residential parcels: a base tax of $249, and an additional $0.195 per square foot of building area above 5,000 square feet, capped at $50,000 per parcel;
  • for non-residential parcels: a base tax of $799, an additional $0.79 per square foot of building area between 5,001 and 50,000 square feet, an additional $0.84 per square foot of building area between 50,001 and 250,000 square feet, and an additional $0.99 per square foot of building area over 250,000 square feet, capped at $400,000 per parcel;
  • for mixed-use parcels: a base tax of $799, and an additional marginal rate tax based on the rates for residential and non-residential parcels, capped at $400,000 per parcel; and
  • for parcels without buildings: a flat tax of $392 if the land area is more than 2,000 square feet.
items.con: A "no" vote opposes creating a property tax, to be in effect from 2027 to 2042, to fund San Francisco Municipal Transportation Agency operations.

items.name: Measure I
items.title: Changes to Real Property Transfer Tax
items.summary: Dedicate 50% of the revenue from the real estate transfer tax to housing and development purposes
items.pro: A "yes" vote supports dedicating 50% of revenue received from the property transfer tax on real estate priced at more than $10 million to affordable housing, including social housing developments, homelessness prevention programs, and housing assistance.
items.con: A "no" vote opposes dedicating 50% of revenue received from the property transfer tax on real estate priced at more than $10 million to affordable housing, including social housing developments, homelessness prevention programs, and housing assistance.

items.name: Measure J
items.title: Removal of Foreclosure Exemption for Real Property Transfer Tax
items.summary: Remove the real estate transfer tax exemption for transfers that occur due to a foreclosure
items.pro: A "yes" vote supports removing the real estate transfer tax exemption for property transfers to the lender in lieu of foreclosure or transfers that take place due to a foreclosure of a property.
items.con: A "no" vote opposes removing the real estate transfer tax exemption for property transfers to the lender in lieu of foreclosure or transfers that take place due to a foreclosure of a property.

items.name: Measure RTM
items.title: Regional Transit Measure
items.summary: Create a sales tax for a 14-year period to fund transportation programs in the region
items.pro:
A "yes" vote supports issuing a sales tax for a period of 14 years to fund public transportation systems in the region, including BART, Muni, Caltrain, AC Transit, Santa Clara Valley Transportation Authority, San Francisco Bay Ferry, and Golden Gate Transit, with the following tax rates:

  • 1.0% in San Francisco; and
  • 0.5% in Alameda, Contra Costa, San Mateo, and Santa Clara counties.
items.con:
A "no" vote opposes issuing a sales tax for a period of 14 years to fund public transportation systems in the region, with the following tax rates:

  • 1.0% in San Francisco; and
  • 0.5% in Alameda, Contra Costa, San Mateo, and Santa Clara counties.
